source_cards.title: The identification power of smoothness assumptions in models with counterfactual outcomes

inspected: Section 1, pages 618–619: conditional counterfactual means and information setting

Section 4, page 630: equation (4.1), distinguishing monotone treatment selection from response monotonicity
not_inspected: Complete supplementary sharpness proofs
Full empirical replication and inference analysis

supports: Conditional-mean response restrictions can be stated separately from individual potential-outcome monotonicity.
Response monotonicity and treatment-selection monotonicity constrain different arguments of the conditional counterfactual mean.
does_not_support: No network, D2/E1, or project certificate theorem is imported from this paper.
The paper's SMTR includes a known Lipschitz bound; the proposed MEAN_ORDER route does not implicitly adopt that smoothness restriction.
SMTR here means smooth monotone treatment response, not Manski (2013)'s semi-monotone treatment response.
The project finite mean-order joint feasible set and sharpness require a separate complete derivation and replay.
source_cards.project_use: Mathematical pre-research supporting explicit mean-level scientific restrictions and terminology; this card is not an implementation or scientific-approval claim.

evidence_rules: Literature metadata or an abstract is not evidence of a fully checked theorem.
A project-derived theorem must be labeled as such and linked to its complete derivation.
A literature card cannot replace independent scientific approval, target binding, or executable replay.
A path to a test is not a claim that the test passed; read the dated result report.
